extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for CVPR 2022 (computer-vision conference peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for how reviewers should evaluate, write, and submit reviews for papers submitted to the CVPR 2022 conference, including ethical, reproducibility, data, and process requirements. Targets assigned reviewers participating in pre-rebuttal, rebuttal, and post-rebuttal stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for what is good or stimulating in the paper and what new knowledge advancement the paper made. Minor flaws that can be easily corrected should not be a reason to reject a paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and potential impact weighed with performance
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend that you embrace novel, brave concepts, even if they have not been tested on many datasets. It is important to weigh both the novelty and potential impact of the work alongside the reported performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that a proposed method does not exceed state-of-the-art accuracy on an existing benchmark dataset is not grounds for rejection by itself. Evaluate novelty/impact in context with empirical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor correctable flaws not grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor flaws that can be easily corrected should not be a reason to reject a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flaws are fixable in revision or camera-ready, note them as weaknesses but do not use them as sole basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / code and checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are highly encouraged to voluntarily submit their code as part of supplementary material. Reviewers may optionally check this code to ensure the paper’s results are reproducible and trustworthy, but are not required to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to use the Reproducibility Checklist as a guide. All code/data should be reviewed confidentially and kept private, and deleted after the review process is complete. Accepted papers are expected (but not required) to submit accompanying code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data contribution (dataset release expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is claiming a dataset release as one of its scientific contributions, it is expected that the dataset will be made publicly available no later than the camera-ready deadline, should it be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate in the corresponding field in the review form whether the paper made such claims and whether the submission form has that field marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of data assets (citation of datasets/code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are advised that they need to cite data assets used (e.g., datasets or code) much like papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a reviewer, carefully check if a paper has adequately cited data assets used in the paper, and comment in the corresponding field in the review form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal data and human subjects (IRB/ethics)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is using personal data or data from human subjects, the authors must have an ethics clearance from an institutional review board (IRB, or equivalent) or clearly describe that ethical principles have been followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no description of how ethical principles were ensured or there are GLARING violations of ethics, inform the Area Chairs and Program Chairs. Reviewers should avoid dealing with such issues by themselves directly. IRB reviews for the US or appropriate local approvals are typically required for new datasets; dataset creators should provide this information when possible. If authors use an existing published dataset, including a discussion of IRB-related issues is encouraged but not required; reviewers should not penalize papers if such a discussion is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of negative societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a discussion on potential negative societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers shall weigh the inclusion of a meaningful discussion POSITIVELY. Reviewers shall NOT reject a paper solely because the paper has not included such a discussion, since there is no formal policy requiring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to explicitly and honestly discuss limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers shall weigh the inclusion of an honest discussion POSITIVELY. A paper is not required to have a separate section to discuss limitations, and absence of a limitations section cannot be the sole factor for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and detailed in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Please be specific and detailed in your reviews. Your main critique should be written in terms of a list of strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single short sentence or a few words do NOT suffice. Use bullet points but explain your arguments. Include specific feedback on ways the authors can improve their papers. Your discussion, more than your score, will help authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis for your recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite references to support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In the discussion of related work and references, simply saying 'this is well known' or 'this has been common practice in the industry for years' is not sufficient: You MUST cite specific publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not provide references to support your claim, the Area Chairs are forced to discount it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media silence / ban during review period
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should NOT use social media to promote their paper submissions to CVPR during the review period (social media silence period defined by dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The silence period is from 10/19/2021 to 03/02/2022. Any social media promotion proactively initiated by the authors during this period is considered a policy violation. Reviewers shall report such cases to Area Chairs and Program Chairs for further investigation; until a conclusion is drawn reviewers should continue reviewing the paper as if there is no violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind review practices and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should make all efforts to keep their identity invisible to the authors and should not attempt to discover authors' identities by searching the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting to arXiv is NOT considered a violation of anonymity by authors. If you know or suspect the authors' identities (e.g., from arXiv), you may still review if you can be impartial. Do not let knowledge of authors affect your judgment; treat papers fairly whether or not you know who wrote them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect ideas / confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must protect the confidentiality of the ideas represented in the papers they review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show the paper, results, videos/images, code, or supplementary material to anyone not asked to help with the review. Do not use ideas/code from papers you review to develop your own work. After the review process, destroy all copies of papers and supplementary material and erase any code and implementations written to evaluate the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid any conflict of interest; there should be absolutely no question about the impartiality of any review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: same institution as an author; directly involved in the work; perception of conflict; collaboration in past three years (e.g., coauthored papers or proposals); being advisor or advisee. If you recognize a conflict, email the Program Chairs as soon as possible and return the paper rather than submit a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Belittling or sarcastic comments have no place in the reviewing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful review. Avoid second-person phrasing; prefer discussing 'the paper' rather than addressing authors directly. Tone matters: a harsh tone will be resented even if criticisms are true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional practical reviewer tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice to write good reviews and behave professionally as a reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take time to read and think before writing. Short reviews are unhelpful. Be specific about unclear sections and suggest clarifications. Be specific about novelty and back claims with references. Do not request authors to cite your papers or give away identity. If a paper seems out of scope, explain why and suggest alternative venues. Be generous with new ideas for improvement. Thoughtful reviews benefit authors and reviewers (e.g., Outstanding Reviewer award).

rubrics_metrics.name: CMT usage and review process steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps reviewers should follow on the CMT site to download, review, discuss, and submit reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Download papers (individually or ZIP). 2) Check for conflicts or submission rule violations and contact Program Chairs if needed. 3) Review papers and assign preliminary (pre-rebuttal) rating using the review form. 4) (Optional) Review offline via XML stubs. 5) Participate in discussions with Area Chairs and other reviewers during post-rebuttal. 6) Enter final (post-rebuttal) recommendation reflecting rebuttal and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is intended to provide details of derivations and results that do not fit within the paper format or space limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary MAY NOT include results obtained with an improved version of the method (e.g., following additional parameter tuning or training), or an updated/corrected version of the submission PDF. Consult supplementary only if helpful; if you find violations, contact the Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal scope and handling of additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may request clarifications or additional illustrations in the rebuttal, but should not request substantial additional experiments for the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per policy, 'substantial' refers to what would be needed in a major revision of a paper. Rebuttals may include figures or comparison tables of results reported in the submission/supplemental material or other papers. Papers should not be penalized for supplying extra results; reviewers can choose to ignore them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a withdrawn dataset is not in itself grounds for rejection, but should invite very close scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should flag use of withdrawn datasets in the review form for AC/PC consideration. Consider: Do the authors explain why they had to do this? Is the explanation compelling? Is there really no alternative dataset? Authors might not know the dataset had been withdrawn. If the paper could be accepted without experiments on the withdrawn dataset, advise authors to remove those experiments. Reviewers/ACs must not require comparison on a withdrawn dataset without consultation with PCs or DEI/ombuds.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv and prior-art treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv preprints are considered pre-publications and are not 'published'; authors are not required to discuss or compare to recent arXiv reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to cite an arXiv paper or failing to beat its performance SHOULD NOT be SOLE grounds for rejection. Reviewers should not reject solely because a similar idea appeared on arXiv. If you suspect plagiarism, report to Program Chairs. Automatic arXiv tweets are not considered author promotion. Project websites and videos are allowed if not posted to social media and if video hosting behaves like a social platform then posts must be comment-disabled and unlisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate each paper on its own (no quota)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no minimum number of papers a reviewer should accept or reject; each paper should be evaluated in its own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you feel most of your assigned papers have value, accept them; if many deserve rejection, provide clear and very specific comments for each. Do NOT assume your stack should match the conference acceptance rate.
